title: Mapping the emerging research landscape on applications of ChatGPT in Language teacher education: a systematic narrative literature review
extended_summary:
This paper examines the emerging empirical literature on ChatGPT in language teacher education, with a focus on how English language teachers use generative AI for instructional support, reflection, professional learning, and student-facing activities. The review was motivated by the rapid uptake of ChatGPT in education and the need to understand both its benefits and its risks, including overreliance, ethical concerns, cultural misalignment, and possible erosion of teacher judgment.

The authors conducted a systematic narrative literature review of 13 peer-reviewed empirical studies published between January 2023 and March 2025. The included studies covered pre-service and in-service English language teachers across a range of contexts, including Türkiye, Iran, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, the United States, and international samples. Study designs included qualitative case studies, phenomenology, mixed-method interventions, and experimental studies. The review synthesized how teachers used ChatGPT for lesson planning, feedback, reflective practice, professional development, and classroom support.

Overall, the review concludes that teachers generally perceive ChatGPT as a useful pedagogical assistant and reflective partner that can reduce workload, support creativity, and improve self-efficacy when used intentionally and with appropriate training. At the same time, the literature consistently warns that the tool can produce repetitive, culturally inappropriate, or inaccurate outputs and may encourage overreliance if used uncritically. The paper argues that ChatGPT should be treated as a mediational tool that augments rather than replaces teacher expertise, and it calls for stronger AI literacy, ethical guidance, and future longitudinal classroom-based research.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot / large language model system used for dialogue, text generation, and assistance with instructional and feedback tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: This systematic narrative review examined empirical studies of English language teachers using ChatGPT for lesson planning, reflective practice, professional development, student feedback, and related instructional support contexts.

findings.finding_summary: Across 13 empirical studies (2023-2025), ChatGPT was generally perceived as helpful for lesson planning, feedback, reflection, and professional development, but the review also identified recurring concerns about overreliance, cultural insensitivity, ethical risks, hallucination/accuracy problems, and contextual misalignment. The review notes that sustained or structured use could improve teacher self-efficacy and instructional competence, but most included studies were short-term and not longitudinal.
findings.measure: Teacher perceptions, instructional use, reflective practice, self-efficacy, and reported pedagogical/ethical concerns across included studies

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic narrative review synthesizing heterogeneous qualitative, mixed-method, and experimental studies rather than a single rigorous trial or meta-analysis. The evidence is useful but indirect for the specific question of negative/null/sustained-use effects, and most included studies were short-term.
impact_tier_rationale: The review reports important practical concerns (overreliance, hallucination, privacy, cultural misalignment) and some positive instructional uses, but it does not provide a single quantified effect size for harm or benefit. Overall impact is plausible but unclear and context-dependent.
